title: Naturality of internal Hom restriction under pre- and post-composition
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with topology $J$, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $U$ an object, and $A,A^\prime,B,B^\prime$ sheaves of $R$-modules [def-pur-sheaf-hom, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Let $f:A^\prime\to A$, $g:B\to B^\prime$, and $F$ be restriction to $U$. Write $c_{A,B}:F\mathcal Hom(A,B)\to\mathcal Hom(FA,FB)$ for the canonical restriction isomorphism. Then $F(\mathcal Hom(f,g))c_{A^\prime,B^\prime}=c_{A,B}\mathcal Hom(Ff,Fg)$.

source.place: Section 04TT (section-internal-hom), sectionwise internal Hom and its restriction maps; Definition 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site)

proof.text: Forget to presheaves of modules. Unfold the fully faithful forgetful functor preimage and the canonical restriction comparison. The final eqToIso has equal objects definitionally, hence its hom is the identity by eqToHom_refl and proof irrelevance. Evaluate at W over U and a section phi. Such a section is a morphism on Over W.left. Apply extensionality to that morphism, at V over W and an element x. The two expressions are definitionally the same composite of the component of f, phi, and g, since restriction and the forward comparison both precompose components. Reflexivity proves the component identity and extensionality proves naturality. This uses no nonemptiness, boundedness, or finiteness assumptions.

proof_origin.description: P2: sectionwise naturality is fully proved in Lean using the concrete canonical comparison, eqToHom_refl, and extensionality.

lean.statement:
theorem overHomObjIso_naturality
    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat.{u})]
    {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (U : C)
    {A A' B B' : SheafOfModules.{u}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat.{u})).obj R)}
    (f : A' ⟶ A) (g : B ⟶ B') :
    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ U).map
        (SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R) f g) ≫
          (SheafOfModules.overHomObjIso A' B' U).hom =
      (SheafOfModules.overHomObjIso A B U).hom ≫
        SheafOfModules.homObjMap (R := R.over U)
          ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ U).map f)
          ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor _ U).map g)
